head: 04da001cb5
scope_text:
This page reviews pull request 4596 of positron-ai/tron at its head commit 04da001cb5 (pushed 2026-09-29 23:57 UTC). The diff base is 66c7bb8db1, the main commit the branch started from. The diff touches 11 files and adds 2,501 lines: the new header h/tron/models/attn_stats.hpp (953 lines), hooks in h/tron/models/self_attention.hpp and h/tron/models/model.hpp, README.stats.md, and six test files including the new t/t_attn_stats.cpp (932 lines). The main branch has moved 161 commits past the base and touches model.hpp and self_attention.hpp. The main-drift lens below checked whether the PR still applies (a lens is one reading pass over the diff with one question in mind).

The review followed the tron-code-review skill (the review checklist this reviewer uses for tron pull requests). The steps applied were:
- trace every execution path the change crosses (forward bookkeeping, visit tallies, timers, the FPGA path, asynchronous ownership, worker and layer indexing)
- check each counter's semantics and owner
- check the relevant conditions
- review whether the tests can fail Nineteen reading lenses produced 128 raw findings. Duplicates were merged. Three independent refuters (checks that try to disprove a finding, here on reachability, on evidence at the head and on intent) checked each merged finding, and a finding was dropped when two of the three refuted it. A completeness critic (a separate pass that looks for review questions the first round missed) chose the seven second-round lenses. The author's 2026-09-30 test-data comments were checked separately (section 'Posted test data').
inspection_text: Every finding below cites line numbers of the head commit 04da001cb5. They shift after the next push. Line numbers of the earlier heads (1430736b2a, the one Wade reviewed) are not used. Each finding states its evidence strength. 'Confirmed by code' means the reviewer quoted the lines that show it. 'Plausible' means one step of the reading was not traced. 'Hypothesis' means the condition's reachability was not shown.
wade_intro: Wade's review of 2026-09-28 (five inline comments at head 1430736b2a) caused the round-4 commits. The table lists each comment, its fix commit, what this review found about the fix, and the findings that concern the same code. This review did not reopen the five decisions. It checked the fixes in their current form at the head.

wade.comment: T5 (join_wait_cycles) was timed only in the hardware join. The software-only poll in run_joins was never timed. So CPU-attention runs read 0.
wade.fix: 6e23101744: run_joins times each period of failed polls with no join progress into join_wait_cycles. Two new test sections.
wade.status: The fix is at the head and both join modes are timed. The author's 2026-09-29 CPU-attention run reads T5 = 4.1 us per decode job (2.1 % of T2). Remaining items are about the wording of what T5 excludes and about the tests. See the related findings.

wade.comment: Two layers wrote the per-forward record (full.hpp for T1 and forwards, model.hpp for the job counts). So another caller of state.forward would give forwards == 0 next to nonzero token_jobs.
wade.fix: b6fd226982: a forward_scope object is constructed first in model::state::forward. It owns T1, the class and the fold. The fold is the destructor step end_forward, which folds the per-token path bits into the record. full.hpp is no longer changed by the PR.
wade.status: The fix is at the head: one owner, constructed at model.hpp:1668. The T1 span moved inside model::state::forward. The related findings concern the PR body sentence that still names the scheduler, and the missing test through model::state::forward.

wade.comment: Per-forward classification puts every serving forward that carries a prompt chunk into prompt_or_mixed. So decode_like shows pure-decode forwards only.
wade.fix: ae8a6d38d9: README sentence plus listener_jobs and kv_only_jobs per class in the forwards leaf. 04da001cb5 adds the three job counts together at the end of the forward.
wade.status: The fix is at the head, and the 2026-09-29 run shows listener_jobs 64 / kv_only_jobs 8,128 for the 8 prefill (prompt-processing) forwards. Per-job tagging stays a follow-up. Related findings are wording items about kv_only.

wade.comment: Range guards in the hooks silently dropped counts. Prefer asserting, and fix the tests to build correctly sized states.
wade.fix: 15f355acb2: every guard is a TRON_ASSERT. note_token_path is deleted. The per-visit bound is one assert per call in token_path_span.
wade.status: The fix is at the head. The abort tests use a fork helper (t/assertion_signal.hpp: it runs the failing call in a forked child process and reports the signal that ended the child, SIGABRT after a failed TRON_ASSERT). Related findings concern which asserts still have no test and the cost of the per-call assert.

wade.comment: Rows were sized by the whole pool but indexed by attention worker. So a per-worker row could mix cores across forwards.
wade.fix: bff317e0d3: rows and path bits are keyed by pool worker. T3/T4 are kept in a per-(class, layer) struct. n_attn_workers min/max are recorded per forward and class.
wade.status: The fix is at the head. The 2026-09-29 run shows pool workers 0 to 6 at zero and 7 to 26 carrying attention rows. Related findings concern the header comment that still says 'per attention worker', the missing sample count for T3, and the observer-worker semantics (the observer is attention worker 0, the one attention worker that records T3 and T4).

testdata_intro: On 2026-09-30 the author posted three comments on the PR: a run of the head on delphi-3bda, the Intel test machine (the qwen-3-4b model, tp2 = tensor parallel over 2 accelerator cards, 8 users, prompt 1024, 256 generated tokens, CPU attention with USE_HW_ATTN=0, the setting that turns the FPGA attention off, and TRON_ATTN_STATS=1), the leaf samples of that run, and the definitions that changed in the last five commits. This section checks the posted numbers against each other and against the code at the head. The arithmetic was recomputed with a script (every derived number in the comments recomputes from the raw counts). In the tables below, 'orchestrator' names the agent that coordinated this review and ran that script, and 'pass (orchestrator)' marks its checks. Four reading passes (called lenses below, each reads the code from one angle) then checked the code-side claims. Two refuters (passes that try to disprove each finding) checked each resulting finding. Verdict words in the claims table: supported_by_both = the posted data and the code at the head both support the claim. supported_by_data or supported_by_code = only the posted data, or only the code, was checked. contradicted = the evidence shows the opposite. not_verifiable = the posted comments do not hold the needed numbers. In the findings, confirmed_by_data = the reviewer quoted the run files that show it.
rejected_intro: These findings were raised by a lens (one review pass that looks for one kind of defect) and dropped by the verifiers (the reviewers who re-check each finding against the code). The reason column below calls the verifiers refuters. They are listed so the reader can see what was considered. The reason column quotes the refuters.
method_text:
Tools: four runs of the Workflow tool (the script runner that starts and sequences Claude subagents). / Main review, first round: 2 mapping agents (test table, change map), 12 lenses (a lens is one review agent that reads the change from one fixed viewpoint), 1 merge planner (an agent that groups duplicate findings into merged findings), 3 refuters (agents that try to disprove a finding) per merged finding (87 first-round findings).
Main review, second round: 1 completeness critic (an agent that looks for areas the first round did not cover), 7 lenses, 1 merge planner, 3 refuters per finding (19 second-round findings). That run used 344 agents in all. The final synthesis agent (the agent that writes the report from the surviving findings) of that run could not emit the full report within its output limit. The report data was therefore assembled in code from the journal (the run's saved record of each step's output). The merge plan was applied. The refuter corrections were applied by majority. Six smaller agents wrote the triage, overview, counter audit, conditions table, proposed tests and verified-correct list. Two refuters checked the two tables that make new claims. / Test-data check: 4 lenses, 17 findings, 2 refuters each, 1 synthesis (39 agents). / Build and test: the head was built and its four test binaries were run on claude-box (the reviewer's build and test container, an AMD host without AMX) by the orchestrator (the workflow script that started the agents) (details under 'Tests actually run'). / Every line number was read at the head by the agent that cites it. The orchestrator did not re-verify every citation. The 'verifier notes' fields carry the refuters' warnings about the findings.

Rules applied to the prose: the plain-English rules of the reviewer's configuration (define terms at first use, one claim per sentence, units on numbers, citations after the sentence, a short version first, no idioms). A separate check pass over this page ran after generation. Its corrections are already applied.

followup_rows.not_caught: The page is passed in `pages`. So estimate_attention_work and finish_sw_plan run for real on the one page. The fixture's run launches no workers. So no attention job executes. The listener buffers are empty (std::monostate). So run_logits skips the wcls matmul (the matrix multiply with the output-word weight matrix, n_logit_chks 0). Only the empty-listener notifications run on the app pool.

followup_short: After the review, five of the seven should-fix items were closed by seven test commits pushed on 2026-09-30 (PR head now 0f784c44ff). The two open items are the stale PR-body performance claims (finding R1-M13 in the Findings section) and the missing T3 sample count (finding R1-M27).
followup_intro: The five should-fix test gaps were closed in this session, after the review above was written. One implementer agent wrote each test against the production boundary named in the finding, ran a deliberate break of the production code to confirm the new assertion fails (a mutation check), reverted the break, and committed. Five reviewer agents then checked each commit with the test questions of the tron-code-review skill (the review checklist used for tron pull requests). Two asked for changes: R1-M8 had bare literals where the C++ guide (the repository's C++ coding guide) asks for named values, and R1-M1 counted listener notifications in a plain integer that two pool workers increment at once (a data race in the test). Both were fixed in follow-up commits. The implementer pushed 4094b51dde before the review step, against its instructions. The two follow-up changes were therefore pushed as new commits (4c70f04604, 0f784c44ff) on top of it. No history was rewritten. Every commit touches test files only: git diff 04da001cb5..0f784c44ff -- h/ is empty.
